A.actClause: AN ACT to amend the public service law, in relation to farm waste net energy metering
A.memo:
BILL NUMBER:A7987A

TITLE  OF BILL:   An act to amend the public service law, in relation to
farm waste net energy metering

PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:  This legislation amends  section  66-j
of  Public  Service law to ensure more equitable net metering provisions
for owners of farm-based anaerobic  or  manure  digesters  in  New  York
State.

SUMMARY  OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:  Section 66-j of the Public Service law
is amended to:

* Amends subsection 1-e the definition of "farm waste electric  generat-
ing equipment" to increase the allowable rated capacity to not more than
one thousand kilowatts.

JUSTIFICATION:    This  legislation  would make needed amendments to net
metering laws as adopted by New York State during the  2008  Legislative
Session  for  anaerobic digesters. These digesters are mostly located on
dairy farms where methane from manure is captured and  used  to  produce
electricity on the farm and, in many cases, net metered back to the grid
for use by others.

The  2008  net-metering law further encourages the development of behind
the meter renewable energy  sources.  These  changes  were  designed  to
further  incentivize  the  development  of renewable energy sources that
individual ratepayers would construct. This helps increase the amount of
renewable energy available in New York  and  reduce  our  dependence  on
fossil  fuels.  However,  there  are  a number of issues that need to be
addressed as a result of the passage of this legislation to ensure  that
the digester technology is treated equitably, when compared to solar and
wind  technologies.  This  bill  seeks  to make these changes, including
expansion of the amount of energy that can be net metered for  anaerobic
digesters.  By  addressing  these  issues, this legislation improves the
state's positive net-metering law for this farm-specific renewable ener-
gy technology and provides both benefits for the environment and renewa-
ble energy production.

PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:  New bill.

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:  None.

EFFECTIVE DATE:  This act shall take effect on the thirtieth  day  after
it shall have become law.
